update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency Indian National Congress (INC) sessions, presidents, and their historical significance for History Static GK.

inc_sessions.significance: The first session of the INC. Attended by 72 delegates. Lord Dufferin was the Viceroy.
The first Muslim President of the INC.
The first English (British) President of the INC.
The national song 'Vande Mataram' (written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee) was sung for the first time.
Formal proclamation of the Swadeshi Movement against the partition of Bengal.
The word 'Swaraj' (Self-Government) was used for the first time from the INC platform.
The infamous 'Surat Split' occurred, dividing the Congress into Moderates and Extremists.
The national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' (written by Rabindranath Tagore) was sung for the first time.
The 'Lucknow Pact' was signed (alliance between INC and Muslim League). Moderates and Extremists were also reunited.
The first Woman President of the INC.
The first and only INC session presided over by Mahatma Gandhi.
The first Indian Woman President of the INC.
Passed the historic 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution. January 26 was declared as Independence Day.
Endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Passed landmark resolutions on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme.
The first INC session to be held in a rural area (village).
A National Planning Committee was set up under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru.
The 'Tripuri Crisis'. Subhas Chandra Bose defeated Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya but resigned shortly after to form the Forward Bloc. Rajendra Prasad took over as President.
He was the President of the INC at the time of India's independence in 1947.
